_what: The RQ4 descriptive layer of the sealed analysis/latency.py, run ONCE over results/raw/latency-pilot.json by the composition root named in DEVIATIONS D-014: every SpanReport from span_descriptives and every ArmPairDelta from arm_pair_delta against B0, as returned. Nothing here is recomputed, selected, or compared to any margin. Refusals are recorded as the sealed layer states them.
corpus: PILOT (fixtures/pilot/golden_thread) -- NOT the confirmatory corpus (D-006, ADR 0047)
cpu_pinning: none; pinning exists only in smoke/g3/spike.py (D-009 / D-014 disclosure)
substrate: in-process harness on one machine (ADR 0034); no network hop is implied

plan.exclusion_rule: NONE. No outlier or stall rule is applied. Sighting C has never been observed as a per-operation stall, so a threshold now would be invented for an effect not shown to exist, and a threshold set after seeing data is what pre-registration forbids. Raw values are reported, not discarded.
plan.ledger_note: the effect ledger is instrument, not mechanism, and ADR 0026 excludes every ledger append from the measured segment by name; `end_to_end` here therefore carries no ledger write
plan.order: arms shuffled within each batch from ORDER_SEED + batch

phase_definition.cold: the first invocation of a freshly provisioned arm instance
phase_definition.warm: a subsequent invocation of that same instance

plan.source: docs/PRE_REGISTRATION.md §6, implemented as written and not amended

Refusal-path latency is its own series: use refusal_span_series()

On that cell the exchange arms perform a failed AS round trip -- which lands in the `delegation` span -- while the capability arms do purely local work, so pooling it with benign cells would average a network refusal together with local cryptography (ADR 0026, §J.3 item 12). Refusal-path latency is its own series: use refusal_span_series()
